title: Next-generation firewall (NGFW) and deep packet inspection

videos.script: Every office writes the same first rule. Staff may browse the web: TCP to ports 80 and 443. {{rule}} In this lesson, that rule lets an SSH session out to a stranger. The session uses port 443, and the rule only ever asked about the port. {{ssh}} A port number is a convention between two programs. Nothing on the wire checks it. {{convention}} So you will read past the headers. Suricata watches the firewall's LAN side and names each conversation by its first bytes. Two flows to port 443 come out as two different protocols. {{flows}} Then you will write a rule that names the application instead of the port, and watch it fire once. {{alert}} Last, you will see what encryption leaves visible to an inspector, and what decrypting on purpose would cost. {{tls}}
